When a senior engineer leaves, the Power Automate flows, Logic Apps and Power BI refreshes running on their account often die with them. This episode is for Microsoft 365 and Azure architects who want automation that survives staff turnover. Learn how to move to service principals, managed identities and federated credentials, scope permissions and automate their life cycle.

In this episode
  • 00:00 – Identity rot: when offboarding breaks automation
  • 00:47 – The shadow account trap
  • 03:54 – Identity as infrastructure: managed identities and federated credentials
  • 07:11 – The permission creep crisis and blast radius
  • 10:00 – Orchestrating the service principal life cycle
  • 13:02 – The zero downtime rotation model
  • 15:58 – The economic reality of identity
  • 18:18 – Homework: find the identity rot

Key takeaways
  • Automations tied to personal or shared service accounts break on offboarding, password changes and MFA, so production workloads need their own service principal identities.
  • Prefer managed identities inside Azure and federated credentials via OpenID Connect for external pipelines, and scope every permission tightly to limit the blast radius.</

Active Directory is far from dead, and a single compromised device can still hand attackers the whole domain. In this conversation for IT admins and security teams, Viktor Hedberg explains AD tiering, privileged access workstations and why getting the basics right beats buying another security tool.

In this episode
  • 00:00 – Introduction and Viktor's path into cybersecurity
  • 03:08 – The biggest identity threats in Active Directory
  • 07:49 – What AD tiering is and what belongs in tier zero
  • 11:43 – Microsoft's shifting guidance on privileged access
  • 18:45 – Dangerous misconceptions about privilege separation
  • 21:06 – How attackers exploit weak tiering and how to respond
  • 28:55 – PAWs, PAM, just-in-time and just enough administration
  • 42:12 – Advice for security teams, passwordless and rapid-fire round

Key takeaways
  • Administrative tiering boxes domain controllers, Entra Connect, PKI and similar systems into tier zero and blocks high-privilege accounts from logging on to lower tiers, limiting credential exposure.

Many organizations buy Copilot licenses and expect instant productivity, only to be disappointed. In this conversation, Microsoft MVP Fabio Bonolo shares with IT professionals and business leaders why change management, data culture and empowering leadership matter more than the tool itself. You get practical tips on champions networks, staying up to date and leading people through AI-driven change.

In this episode
  • 00:00 – Meet Fabio Bonolo and his path into Microsoft
  • 03:38 – The future of work and the end of the clicking culture
  • 06:28 – Modern work, change management and measuring productivity
  • 11:50 – Copilot, data quality and data culture
  • 20:29 – Keeping up with updates and building champions
  • 27:59 – Leadership, empowerment and communication
  • 46:02 – Avoiding burnout: find your niche
  • 50:29 – Community events and final thoughts

Key takeaways
  • AI and Copilot projects succeed when organizations invest in change management, training and enablement alongside the technology.</
